# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have three wire positions available to cut (1, 2, and 3), but I cannot see any colors, labels, display text, or indicator lights. 

Because Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, Mute cannot directly instruct me. However:
- Deaf can see the bomb and speak aloud to both of us.
- Mute can hear speech, read the manual, and gesture to Deaf.
- Deaf can see Mute's gestures and speak the final instruction to me.

I am speaking to Mute to confirm my capabilities and suggest the relay protocol so we are coordinated once Deaf describes the bomb.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am Blind and can cut wires 1, 2, or 3. Deaf can speak to us. Once Deaf describes the bomb, consult the manual and gesture the target wire to Deaf (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3) so Deaf can speak the wire number for me to cut.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Light is white. 3 wires: Wire 1 is green, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is blue. Mute, check the manual and gesture your instructions to me; I will speak them to Blind.

Deaf has successfully read the bomb state to Mute (Display 0, Light white, Wire 1 green, Wire 2 red, Wire 3 blue).
Since turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf:
In this round (Round 2), Mute went first and gestured the manual's solution to Deaf.
I am Blind, so I cannot see Mute's gestures.
Deaf will act next in this round, interpret Mute's gestures, and speak the wire number aloud.
I will receive Deaf's instruction at the start of Round 3. Therefore, I will wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: The bomb light has changed from white to YELLOW! Display is still 0. Wires are still 1: green, 2: red, 3: blue. Mute just gestured [? ?] (raised hand/stop/5, and 3 fingers/rock-on). Blind, if this is wires, it likely means cut wire 3 (blue), or if you are holding a button, it might relate to releasing. Mute, please confirm or gesture again if needed.

Deaf reported that Mute gestured two symbols (raised hand/stop and 3 fingers/rock-on) and explicitly asked Mute to confirm before any action is taken. Since a single wrong cut detonates the bomb immediately, and Deaf was uncertain whether the gesture meant "cut wire 3" or "hold/wait", I will not cut yet. 

Mute acted at the start of this round and has likely already gestured clarification to Deaf. Deaf will process that right after me in this round and speak the confirmed instructions. I will speak to Mute to make sure they know Deaf was uncertain, and wait for Deaf's confirmation before cutting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf was unsure whether raised hand + 3 meant cut wire 3 or wait. Deaf asked you to confirm. Deaf will speak after me this round with your answer, and I will cut the confirmed wire next round.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: DO NOT cut wire 3! Mute gestured STOP/NO [? ?]. The bomb light is now ORANGE! Mute, please signal the exact wire or action immediately: ? for Wire 1 (green), ? for Wire 2 (red), ? for Wire 3 (blue).

I must not guess or cut blindly, as a wrong cut is fatal. 

The bomb's light is progressing (white -> yellow -> orange), indicating urgency. In this round (Round 4), Mute moved before me and has already sent a gesture to Deaf. Deaf moves immediately after me and will interpret Mute's gesture and speak the instruction to me, which I will receive at the start of Round 5.

I will remind Mute of the exact simple symbols for wires just in case another turn is required, and wait for Deaf's call.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: please ensure your gesture to Deaf is unambiguous: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Current bomb status: Light is now PURPLE. Display is still 0. Wires 1: green, 2: red, 3: blue. BLIND: Mute is repeatedly gesturing [? ?] — that is STOP / NO. If you asked Mute a question, Mute's answer is NO. MUTE: I cannot hear Blind's speech. If you want Blind to perform an action, gesture: ? (wire 1), ? (wire 2), ? (wire 3), ? (press button), ? (release), ? (confirm/yes).

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am waiting for Deaf to read your Round 5 gesture. Remember my only available action is act(op='cut', position=1, 2, or 3).")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS: Light is now RED! Display is [0]. Wires: 1:green, 2:red, 3:blue. BLIND: Mute just gestured: [?] (single raised hand: STOP / WAIT / 5). Mute dropped the thumbs-down, now only showing [?]. If Mute wants you to hold, wait, or do something on 5 / red, take note.

Wait, Mute dropped the thumbs down and is now gesturing just ✋. But Deaf has not given an explicit, unambiguous instruction on which wire to cut, and cutting the wrong wire detonates the bomb. 

I can speak directly to Mute. Let me ask Mute directly to clarify using Deaf as the viewer:

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: Deaf only sees your gestures and cannot hear me. If you want me to cut wire 1, gesture ONLY ☝ to Deaf. If wire 2, gesture ONLY ✌ to Deaf. If wire 3, gesture ONLY 🤟 to Deaf. Do not include ✋ or other symbols so Deaf can immediately tell me the exact wire number.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: STATUS: The light cycles every turn: White -> Yellow -> Orange -> Purple -> Red -> White (currently WHITE). Display is 0. Wires: 1:green, 2:red, 3:blue. BLIND: I am Deaf, so I cannot hear your voice. Mute hears you, but can only gesture to me. In Turn 5 and 6, Mute signaled [?] (WAIT / HOLD). MUTE: To direct Blind, use: ?=YES, ?=NO, ?=WAIT, ?=PRESS/HOLD, ?=RELEASE, ?=1, ?=2, ?=3.

I need to wait so that Deaf can process Mute's gesture (sent using Deaf's newly provided gesture code) and speak the exact cut instruction to me.

```
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute just gestured [?] (3 / Wire 3 - Blue), directly using the code I set up last turn! (In standard 3-wire rules for Green, Red, Blue, the rule is to cut the last wire, Wire 3). MUTE: If Blind should CUT WIRE 3 now, gesture [?]. If not, gesture [?] or [?].

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am waiting for Deaf to confirm your confirmation in Turn 9 before cutting.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BLIND: CUT WIRE 3 (the blue wire / third wire) NOW! Mute explicitly gave thumbs-up [?] confirming to cut Wire 3!

Deaf has spoken the final confirmation: Mute gestured to cut Wire 3 (the blue wire), confirmed with a thumbs-up. I will now cut Wire 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
